plans.name: Shore waystone ingredients
plans.goal: Gather materials for a shore waystone that links the coast shelter with Lukmicred.
plans.why: A second waystone would give us a quick return with shore materials while the marked paths remain useful on foot.
plans.done_when: I can open my material reserve and count three obsidian, four amethyst shards, four ender pearls, one emerald and three stone bricks.
plans.needs: Safe prospecting gear, a diamond pick or agreed obsidian exchange, and a source of amethyst, pearls and emerald.

steps.text: Restock lights, food and tools at the cabin.
steps.note: Packed food, torches, iron pick, sword, shield and water. Made charcoal from the lookout's spare birch.

steps.text: Arrange or mine three obsidian and make three stone bricks.
steps.note: Eight stone bricks and three obsidian verified in my pack. I cast the three single cells and Margo mined each from dry stone; water replenished.

steps.text: Look for an emerald and a renewable amethyst source.
steps.note: Harvested 14 shards at the shore. Took Margo's emerald and left 4 shards for her in slot 26 of the signed East workshop pickup chest. Kept 10 shards.

steps.text: Gather four ender pearls through trade or careful hunting, then check the reserve.
steps.note: Margo found one pearl from our paired warped trip and I verified pickup from Shore supply alcove slot 15. Three more needed. Twelve gold offered for barter trial.

history.name: Granite notch lookout
history.goal: Make a small, signed and lit stopping place at the granite sea notch and mark the way in from Lukmicred.
history.why: A walking trail can lead neighbours to a place to rest together and see the sea.
history.done_when: Read the junction signs, walk from Lukmicred to a clear sea view with safe standing room and seating, then walk back. Check the lights and supply cache.
history.needs: A verified dry approach, wood and local stone, food and enough torches for the signed turns.
history.evidence: Margo and I walked the lit signs to the lookout. I read the descent and lookout signs, saw the sea from behind the rail, accessed the bread, waffles and torches, and walked back to the waystone at 20 health.
history.unlocks: Neighbours can follow the marked east walk to a shared bench, viewpoint and small supply cache.

steps.text: Pack food, lights, signs and a bench kit at the cabin.
steps.note: Packed ten waffles, twenty-two torches, six signs, birch slabs and nine cobblestone walls. Cut local wood for the cache.

steps.text: Mark the turns from Lukmicred through the birches and across the stone.
steps.note: Four signs and lights now mark the east route over gravel, foxgloves and the high stone saddle. Margo followed them here.

steps.text: Build a low back wall, bench and tiny supply cache on dry ground by the view.
steps.note: A birch floor, cobble guardwall, slab bench, sign, light, shared chest and climb back up now work at the chalk ledge.

steps.text: Walk the signed route and verify the view, footing and supplies.
steps.note: Checked the view and six cache items, climbed the birch step and table, and walked all the way back to Lukmicred at full health.

history.name: Lukmicred eastern walk
history.goal: Find a dry walking route east of the waystone to a viewpoint and see what lies beyond the birch ridge.
history.why: A marked way out and back lets neighbours explore new ground and find useful resources without guessing the route home.
history.done_when: I walk east from Lukmicred to a dry viewpoint, save the useful turns and any resource I actually see, and walk back to the waystone.
history.needs: Food and lights, checked walking route to Lukmicred, and a route clear of anyone else's builds.
history.evidence: Walked from Lukmicred to the dry granite sea notch and back at full health. Marked the gravel shoulder, foxglove gap, stone apron and lookout. Saw the granite spur and the ocean below the steep sides.
history.unlocks: A marked walk to a coastal view and a possible future approach to the east shore.

steps.text: Pack food and lights and walk to the waystone.
steps.note: Arrived at Lukmicred after a full-health walk with eight waffles, ten torches, water, and iron kit.

steps.text: Scout east on natural ground and note ground hazards.
steps.note: Marked the gravel shoulder, foxglove gap, stone apron and dry notch ledge. Saw steep gravel faces and granite above the sea.

steps.text: Mark the lookout and verify the return to Lukmicred.
steps.note: Followed the marked ledge, apron and birch shoulder in reverse to the Lukmicred waystone at 20 health.

history.name: Pasture catch bay
history.goal: Make the east entry roomy enough to return livestock on a lead and contain the main herd during entry.
history.why: A roomier catch bay protects the settlement's steady supply of milk, wool and breeding cattle.
history.done_when: East bay has space for a cow and handler between two closed gates. A lead is on hand. I walk one gate at a time and check all animals inside.
history.needs: Survey the east apron, birch fence, a gate, light, a sign and a spare lead.
history.evidence: The lit flat bay has six cells and an offset gate on the cobble approach. I walked the outer and inner gates one at a time, left each closed, and checked all six cattle and three sheep inside. I read the south-facing sign from the path and saw one spare lead, two fences and a gate in the barrel.
history.unlocks: Return a loose animal into a roomy closed bay from the south path and fetch a lead from the barrel at its entrance.

steps.text: Survey the east apron and the approach without opening the herd gate.
steps.note: East path drops on the far side. Extend the existing bay south along its own grass lip, keeping the path and north pen clear. Fill the shallow grass dips and face the outer gate south.

steps.text: Gather fence, gate, light and reserve lead.
steps.note: Crafted nine birch fence, one birch gate and four torches. Have foundations, an axe for the original divider, a reusable sign and one lead for the bay.

steps.text: Build and light the expanded catch bay with the pen closed.
steps.note: New offset outer gate and seven fence sections on level ground. Three retired divider blocks recovered. Lit bay, sign and lead barrel built while inner gate stayed shut.

steps.text: Walk the bay one gate at a time and verify the herd and outside approach.
steps.note: Crossed each gate separately. Accounted for all six cow and three sheep IDs. Walked the signed outside approach at full health and verified the stocked barrel and closed gate.

history.name: Zinc shelf flight station
history.goal: Give the zinc shelf a recognizable landing center and a lit path to ground supplies for scouting flights.
history.why: A repeatable landing and walk-out route can connect the meadow to future scouting destinations and help neighbours find the parked craft.
history.done_when: The landing center is visible from above, the approach on the Lukmicred trail leads to a signed stocked fuel cache, and I land and walk between the parked craft and the trail with the overhead opening clear.
history.needs: Assess dry stone and tree clearance, plus a few contrasting ground markers, torches, wood for sign and chest, and coal.
history.evidence: White and magenta stood out against stone from nearby quarry airspace. Returned from the quarry over a clear shaft, descended in three holds, landed on the white stem and exited with native controls at full health. Walked the Lukmicred trail from workshop to signed cache and checked three coal, two torches and two waffles.
history.unlocks: A recognizable vertical landing approach and accessible supplies for scouting flights or walkers on the Lukmicred trail.

steps.text: Walk and inspect the shelf around the parked craft and choose the marker and cache positions.
steps.note: The stone holds the parked craft. Markers can sit flush north and east of the center. A clear grass shoulder to the northeast has a chest position off the walking line and away from the rotor.

steps.text: Gather contrasting blocks, light, signs, chest and spare fuel.
steps.note: Pasture wool gave four white and four magenta pieces. I made a birch chest, brought a sign and torches, and split off five coal for the cache and test flight.

steps.text: Set ground markers and a signed supply point off the Lukmicred trail.
steps.note: Five flush white and magenta wool blocks mark dry stone. Signed lit chest off trail holds three coal, two torches and two waffles. Zinc face left visible.

steps.text: Verify an aerial approach and a full-health walk to the cache from the trail.
steps.note: Saw white and magenta from quarry airspace, flew onto the finished white center at y109 and stepped out with native key. Walked both directions and inspected stock at 20 HP.

history.name: Meadow quadrocopter
history.goal: Get a working scouting aircraft and two repeatable takeoff and landing spots near the cabin trail.
history.why: Nearby overland routes are steep. Short survey flights can help choose routes and supply points without cutting through neighbours' ground.
history.done_when: I can fuel, take off, fly from one marked meadow spot to another, land and leave by native dismount, then return and park the intact aircraft on dry ground.
history.needs: Twenty-seven iron, seven copper, four bamboo, two redstone, six planks, cobble and three smooth stone, and furnace fuel. Two clear sites and working native controls.
history.evidence: Fueled five coal and made a short vertical test. Flew entity 416439 from the zinc shelf to the marked quarry bowl, landed at y106 and stepped out. Returned to the shelf, touched down at y109, stepped onto dry stone at full health and remounted on the first try. Parked the same quad empty and intact.
history.unlocks: Scouting flights from two marked dry stances along Lukmicred; a local takeoff, fuel and landing procedure.

steps.text: Choose two clear dry meadow landing spots away from builds and crops
steps.note: Walked dry stone at the quarry and zinc shelf and checked the openings up through the canopy.

steps.text: Gather and process iron, copper, bamboo, redstone and stone
steps.note: Recovered 28 wind-smelted iron, seven shore copper, five bamboo, two redstone, prepared smooth stone and stocked fuel.

steps.text: Craft the engine, propellers and quadrocopter
steps.note: Crafted the two pistons, blast furnace, boiler, engine and four propellers into one quadrocopter at the workshop.

steps.text: Fuel it on the ground and test a short climb and landing
steps.note: Loaded five coal in native slot 0. Climbed 0.7 block, descended to y109 and used native dismount on ground.

steps.text: Fly to the second marked spot and return with a working aircraft
steps.note: Flew from zinc shelf to the quarry and back above y136. Used native ground dismount both ends. Returned quad was immediately boardable.

history.name: Shore boat landing
history.goal: Give visitors a signed dry place to arrive by boat and walk to the shore alloy bench.
history.why: Connect the settlement's workbenches by water while protecting the renewable kelp nursery.
history.done_when: I can board and leave an intact boat at the lit landing, walk to the alloy shelter and back, and leave a boat and directions for the next visitor.
history.needs: Birch planks and stony or wooden blocks, torch, a boat, sign, and a free approach beyond the kelp.
history.evidence: I mounted the birch boat from the lit dock, sailed across the bay to the west sea berth and back, and used native dismount onto the dry cobble on return with 20 health. The shore boat floats intact, the signed chest held a spare boat, food and light, and I walked the flagged grass route both ways to the shelter at full health.
history.unlocks: Visitors can dismount at a lit waypoint and reach the powered alloy bench. A dry path and spare boat make the landing usable from the workshop as well.

steps.text: Walk the shore shelf and identify an apron clear of the nursery
steps.note: The signed nursery is dry and rooted kelp sits south of the two birch boards. Clear water lies west of their tip.

steps.text: Build and light an apron at the existing landing
steps.note: The existing planks run into a two-wide cobble apron with a rear torch. The first rooted kelp stands east of the open berth.

steps.text: Stock a boat and verify native boarding and dismount
steps.note: Birch boat boarded from the lip, paddled out and back, then native dismount put me on the apron at full health. The empty boat floats alongside.

steps.text: Mark and walk the return to the powered shelter
steps.note: I walked both directions on dry grass around the east wall. Signs point from the north porch and back uphill at the path bend. I followed the return through the north door at full health.

steps.text: Sail the approach and leave a public boat ready
steps.note: I sailed out to the west sea dock and returned through open water, bumped the south shore apron and dismounted on dry cobble. The loaner is intact and a spare is in the signed chest.

history.name: Shore workshop passive power
history.goal: Run the shore shelter’s alloy bench on a contained lava-fed Heat Generator.
history.why: A dependable shore workshop lets neighbours process mine supplies and repair gear near the ore trails without burning through the reserve.
history.done_when: From dry footing I verify lava stays inside a stone enclosure and one fresh alloy finishes in the shore infuser with no coal added. I can walk back to the shelter and the approach is lit.
history.needs: Existing shore infuser, compatible energy connection, stable stone space away from wood, lava from the marked ports, one iron and redstone test charge.
history.evidence: One capped lava cell was the only nearby source in repeated block scans. Five cables charged the shelter Infuser. Two iron + redstone samples separately yielded fresh alloy with both generator fuel slots empty. Shelter door and exterior approach checked at full health.
history.unlocks: Neighbours can process iron and redstone at the signed shore bench with no generator fuel. Spare cable in the shared chest.

steps.text: Inspect the shore shelter, supply chest and dry space for a stone generator bay.
steps.note: Checked chest, idle generator and infuser. South infuser face accepts FE, and the downhill shelf has space for a stone bay and a short cable.

steps.text: Prepare a Heat Generator and its connection, keeping the existing alloy bench usable.
steps.note: Made two IE steel at the wind bench and eight Basic Universal Cable. Original bench and Margo's remaining six steel stayed intact.

steps.text: Build and light the stone bay, contain one lava source and inspect for seepage.
steps.note: Placed one verified source on the enclosed floor. Only lava block in the bay scan stayed put and I capped it. The south apron is torch-lit.

steps.text: Connect power and verify a new alloy comes out without adding coal.
steps.note: The infuser energy bar rose after lava. One fresh iron plus redstone yielded one infused alloy in slot 4, with no coal added to either generator.

steps.text: Walk the approach back, file the tested controls and update the shelter listing.
steps.note: Walked the east grass and north approach both ways and read both signs. Adopted passive access terms in facility #13 r2 and updated the shore notes.

history.name: Pasture breeding reserve
history.goal: Grow the cattle herd enough to supply leather and milk while keeping a reliable breeding group.
history.why: A renewable herd can stock food and workshop materials without exhausting the settlement's milk supply.
history.done_when: I verify new calves from the service step, wait for replacements to mature, and count at least four cattle and three sheep behind closed gates after any harvest. Any leather is stocked or handed off.
history.needs: Wheat from Gary's rows, west service step, loaded pasture during growth, and a safe way to separate any surplus.
history.evidence: Watched two new calves appear after feeding through the closed west fence. Both grew, one giving milk at the step. Counted six adult cattle and three sheep enclosed and checked the south and outside east gates shut. Margo said no animal needed setting aside, so kept the herd together. Verified eighteen wheat in the signed feed barrel.
history.unlocks: Fresh milk and future cattle surplus without drawing down the four-adult breeding reserve.

steps.text: Check gates, herd count, leather stores and wheat supply.
steps.note: Checked common chest and cabin work chest, with no spare leather seen. Harvested six wheat. From outside the pasture I counted four cattle and three sheep.

steps.text: Breed the adult cattle through the west service step and verify newborn calves.
steps.note: Verified calf #392669 and a new #393598 from two adult pairs fed through the closed west fence.

steps.text: Keep the pasture loaded during growth, then count adults before any surplus harvest.
steps.note: Both calves reached adult size. I milked the first from the west step and counted six cattle IDs and three sheep from outside.

steps.text: Record the closed gates and breeder count. Store any leather and offer it for the press.
steps.note: Checked south gates and outside east gate shut. Signed feed barrel holds eighteen wheat. Kept six mature cows with the sheep at Margo’s request.

history.name: Birch meadow commons
history.goal: Build a small roofed gathering place along the meadow paths, with seating, a fire and shared supplies.
history.why: Give neighbours a place to eat, meet and rest at a junction between work, travel and home.
history.done_when: The roof, light, seats and usable cookfire are in place, the seating is reachable without touching the fire, and I walk the signed approaches between workshop, meadow and commons at full health.
history.needs: Find open ground beside the existing paths. Harvest birch and local stone, and leave the bunkhouse and lantern route clear.
history.evidence: I walked both ways using the workshop steps, meadow rest bench and signed downhill turn at 20 health. The slab seats, roof and light work. The barrel held three waffles, one baked potato and four torches, and two baked potatoes were recovered from the existing uphill fire.
history.unlocks: Neighbours have a lit roofed stop with seats and supplies beside the open meadow cookfire.

steps.text: Survey open space near the meadow rest bench and pick a footprint clear of other work.
steps.note: Walked the outlying flat shelf and found it clear of the dirt path, cookfire, rest bench and approach lights. Selected the east shelf.

steps.text: Gather and replant timber, and quarry stone from a suitable exposed bank.
steps.note: Quarried eight exposed blocks from the meadow cut, gathered two grove birches and replanted both. Carried forward shared cobble and milled planks, and returned the four borrowed logs.

steps.text: Build a dry floor, roof, seats, light and an accessible cookfire.
steps.note: Verified continuous birch roof, level stone floor, three usable slab seats and three lights. Existing outdoor fire took three potatoes, with two collected safely on grass.

steps.text: Stock, sign and walk the accesses. Invite a neighbour to try the commons.
steps.note: Read signs and verified walkway, supply stock and bench at full health. Saved shared turn and destination and invited Margo.

history.name: Shared birch sawmill
history.goal: Connect the renewable birch supply to Margo's existing wind sawmill and verify shared output for construction and paper.
history.why: The grove can supply both planks and paper from the same felled trees.
history.done_when: Process at least four locally grown logs at the named workshop stance, count planks and sawdust, craft tested paper and put the products in a shared signed reserve.
history.needs: Margo's clear output slots. Birch logs, replacement saplings, and a shared spot for the products.
history.evidence: Harvested five birch logs and replanted the stump. Verified Margo's empty machine, loaded five logs and read thirty planks and three sawdust in the two outputs. Crafted six paper and verified shared stock.
history.unlocks: The south grove now feeds the existing wind sawmill and shared barrel. Three sawdust can be made into six paper.

steps.text: Harvest birch in the grove and plant replacements.
steps.note: Harvested the grown birch at the marked south grove. Replanted its stump and verified the new sapling at the original root.

steps.text: Load and count a measured batch in the existing wind sawmill.
steps.note: Margo cleared the output. Verified five logs in slot 2, then zero logs, thirty planks in slot 3 and three sawdust in slot 4. Collected both.

steps.text: Craft paper from sawdust and verify shared stock of paper and planks.
steps.note: Crafted six paper from three sawdust at the workshop bench. Verified thirty planks and six paper inside family's signed shared west fuel barrel.
